episodes.212045: An isolated thunderstorm produced a tornado in Columbus County, NC.
episodes.212046: Scattered thunderstorms developed ahead of a cold front, initially from the southwest associated with a subtle shortwave and then from the west ahead of the front itself. Isolated wind damage with multiple hail reports (quarter to golf ball sized) in northern Horry.
episodes.212533: Multiple rounds of storms moved over portions of SE Texas, bringing large hail and damaging winds.
episodes.212699: Thunderstorms developed during the afternoon hours. One particular storm became severe and produced isolated wind damage.
episodes.212744: Severe winds on this date were driven by a southeastward-moving shortwave trough that had overspread the region while a surface low over northwest Texas, an advancing cold front, and a dryline provided the focus for thunderstorm initiation. Strong daytime heating beneath steep mid-level lapse rates and a moist Gulf air mass produced moderate to strong instability, with MLCAPE values generally ranging from 2,500 to 3,500 J/kg. To our north and west, initial storms developed as supercells capable of producing very large hail, but we anticipated rapid upscale growth into a forward-propagating mesoscale convective system (MCS) and bowing line segment by the time the system reached our CWA. The combination of abundant instability, a dry mid-level air mass, and strengthening forcing aloft favored the development of a strong cold pool, allowing the convective system to accelerate south-southeastward across South Texas. As storms merged and became increasingly outflow-dominant, widespread damaging straight-line winds produced corridors of significant wind damage as the system advanced toward the Texas Coast overnight.

episodes.213022: Over Mother's Day weekend, a slow-moving cold front triggered scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms across North and Central Texas. The majority of these storms occurred on Mother's Day (May 10), with many reaching severe levels and large hail becoming the most frequent report. Hail up to 4.5 was reported in Hamilton County.
episodes.213220: A cold front moved across South-Central Texas on the evening of May 10, encountering an unstable airmass and producing a line of strong to severe storms with damaging wind gusts and some severe hail. Most of the  observed wind damage occurred in the Austin area.
episodes.213322: A weak cold front tracked across Eastern North Carolina during the morning and afternoon hours of May eleventh. As the front tracked across the coastal waters of Eastern North Carolina, widely scattered showers and thunderstorms developed along the coast with an isolated storm or two becoming strong in nature. The strongest storm that developed produced a waterspout in the Core Sound given the favorable environment.
episodes.213824: A moist and moderately unstable airmass along a cold front moving through the region  supported development of thunderstorms across southeast Louisiana late afternoon and evening of May 11th. Although weak low-level flow limited the overall severe-weather organization, locally heavy rainfall occurred in Baton Rouge metro as well as a brief tornado and associated wind damage in St. James Parish near Grand Point and Paulina.
episodes.214060: The combination of a dryline and cold front along with strong instability resulted in scattered severe thunderstorms across much of the area. The strongest storms produced very large hail and damaging winds.
episodes.214075: A cold front stalled across the region while multiple short waves moved overhead. This produce multiple days of unsettled weather.
episodes.214226: Isolated thunderstorms developed in the afternoon hours along the southeast South Carolina coast. One storm in Beaufort County became strong enough to produce hail.
